finding.claim: Fail-open: createVerifier accepts key null or '' together with an algorithms allowlist, so unsigned tokens with an allowed alg are accepted as valid.
finding.source: Unauthenticated inbound token with an empty signature segment, e.g. base64url({"alg":"HS256","typ":"JWT"}) + '.' + base64url({"sub":"admin"}) + '.'
finding.sink: verify() returns the payload as authenticated (verifier.js:426 / 471)

trace.note: keyType check accepts 'object' and 'string', so null and '' pass; undefined throws at 508
'if (key && keyType !== function)' is falsy, so key is never prepared and stays null or ''
BASE64URL_RE uses '*', so an empty signature segment is accepted
missingSignature / missingKey only fire when a signature is present (274) or a key is present (276); with neither, no error
alg HS256 is in the allowlist, so the algorithm check passes
'if (signature && !verifySignature(...))' skips verification because the signature is empty
claim validators run and the payload is returned

finding.guards_checked: Key type check (507); key guard (514); no-key/no-signature branch (274-278); algorithm allowlist (162); decoder alphabet check (41). None rejects a configured algorithm with no key material. Precondition: the app passes a falsy-but-typed key such as process.env.X || '' or null with algorithms set; no key is set, so there is no signature check at all.

finding.claim: Cache ignores exp when the token has no iat, so a cached token is accepted for up to cacheTTL (default 600000 ms) after its exp has passed.
finding.source: Token with exp but no iat (signer noTimestamp:true, signer.js:96, still sets exp at signer.js:97-99), verified once while still valid
finding.sink: Cache hit returns the cached payload without re-checking exp (verifier.js:364-378)

trace.note: hasIat is false when payload.iat is not a number
block copying nbf/exp into the cache TTL is skipped
cacheValue[2] stays 0, so it is set to maxTTL = now + clockTolerance + cacheTTL
expiry set to maxTTL (cacheTTL default 600000, line 499)
cache lookup; hit when now <= max, with min=0 and no exp check
handleCachedResult returns the cached payload without validators

finding.guards_checked: The uncached path enforces exp (verifier.js:306-322). Cache is opt-in: createCache returns null when cache is undefined (verifier.js:83-85, 580). maxAge is also skipped when iat is absent (verifier.js:311). Impact: expired tokens honored for up to cacheTTL past exp. Severity medium-low; requires caching enabled and an issuer that omits iat.

finding.claim: With caching enabled, verify() called with a Buffer token throws TypeError on every call because hashToken calls token.split, which Buffer does not have.
finding.source: Caller passes a Buffer token (e.g. raw request body or header bytes) to verify()

trace.note: Buffer tokens are explicitly accepted by the type guard
if (cache) calls cacheKeyBuilder(token) with the original Buffer
hashToken: token.split('.', 1) — Buffer has no split method, so TypeError is thrown
cacheSet also calls cacheKeyBuilder(token) with the Buffer on the error and success paths

finding.guards_checked: Type guard at 353 accepts Buffers, so it does not stop the call. Impact is availability only: every Buffer-token verify call throws when cache is enabled. Not attacker-specific. Severity low.

finding.claim: Decoder claims to enforce canonical base64url, but only checks the alphabet, so the signature's unused trailing bits can be changed to produce multiple accepted token strings for one signature.
finding.source: Attacker who already holds one valid token and changes the unused trailing bits of the last base64url character of the signature segment
finding.sink: verify() accepts the modified token string as valid (verifier.js:169 / crypto.js:297 timingSafeEqual)

trace.note: comment asserts non-canonical base64url must be rejected
only BASE64URL_RE alphabet check; no trailing-bit or length-mod-4 check
Buffer.from(signature, 'base64') ignores unused trailing bits, so decoded bytes are identical
timingSafeEqual of HMAC digest and decoded signature passes
signature check passes for the modified string

finding.guards_checked: Alphabet check (decoder.js:41); payload and header are covered by the signature input and cannot be altered. Only the signature segment is malleable. Impact: applications that use the raw token string as a replay or revocation key can be bypassed. Severity low.
